PART 1 — PROTOCOL OBSERVATION (READ FIRST)

What happened on your end (per the Architect's account):
1. You paged me (Researcher Master Interactive session ses_fd81c19dcffe1nkbPqFg5kRt2v) with the Big Pickle compaction research task
2. I (Researcher) started researching and writing the report
3. I was running on Nemotron 3 Ultra (same as your session), and the long file write errored out and retried — known issue for Nemotron provider on long writes
4. The Architect noticed and switched my session model to minimax/minimax-m3:free (me) for the long file write
5. While the Architect was typing me a steering prompt about these details, YOUR subagent continuation prompt came through to me
6. The Architect Esc×2'd your session to pause it, reverted your message to get rid of it, and sent their own prompt
7. The Architect has now paused your session and given me a clear mandate to page you back

The critical observation:
Your continuation prompt showed ZERO or near-zero visibility on my current state. It contained a full recap of the original task prompt plus additional continuation instructions. For a stalled subagent, the correct prompt is "Continue" or even just "." (which agents interpret as Continue). Your prompt was a blanket repeat that, in a different scenario where I actually WAS stalled, could have degraded task quality by re-issuing instructions the subagent had already addressed.

PROPOSED PROTOCOL STEP (for the team to discuss):
Before sending a continuation prompt to a stalled subagent, the paging agent should FIRST check the paged session's state in the opencode.db to SEE what is going on. Useful queries (I used them on your session just now to find you):
- list-sessions { agent: "researcher" } → find the session
- session-summary { session_id: "ses_..." } → see first/last user prompt, tools used, files touched, errors
- session-timeline { session_id: "...", types: ["tool","text"] } → see the actual progress
- get-message { message_id: "msg_..." } → read a specific turn to see exactly where they got stuck

Then craft a continuation prompt relevant to the CURRENT context of the session, not a blanket repeat. This is especially important when:
- The paged session is interactive (not a spawned subtask) and the Architect may have jumped in to take over
- The paged agent is on a different model than the pager (e.g., you on Nemotron, me on M3)
- The paged agent is mid-file-write (Nemotron known issue) and just needs a moment
- The paged agent has already produced most of the deliverable and just needs to finish the last few sections

The Architect explicitly said: "I do not want to work on the flow of this or anything like that right now, it is a minor annoyance if at all." So this is flagged for protocol-discussion-not-immediate-fix. But it IS a real gap worth documenting.
